Outbox ingestBatch pseudocode:

reviewFindings: OT1-G1 (rank4): oas Adapter interface (src/core/types.ts) is internal, not a versioned public SDK — separate repo makes internal refactors silent breaking changes for oas-command-stats.
OT1-G2 (rank3): cross-repo release coordination latency for adapter bug fixes (hours-days vs monorepo single-PR).
OT1-G3 (rank3): drill-down workflow couples oas+oas-stats binaries; version skew silently breaks session handoff.
LD2-G1 (rank5, SOPHISTICATED): ts-based high-watermark permanently drops late/out-of-order events (NTP skew, retroactive edits, compaction appends) — canonical CDC trap.
LD2-G2 (rank4): watermark JSON not crash-safe; 10 concurrent PromisePool workers race on it; no atomic write specified.
LD2-G3 (rank4): session_id reuse (reinstall/test/copy/zcode regen) invalidates 'fully-ingested → skip' — no content fingerprint in watermark key.
LD2-G4 (rank4): pi compaction event type + JSONL rotation/truncation breaks watermark event_count/last_event_id assumptions.
LD2-G5 (rank3): cmd_events has no event_id column; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING target unspecified → false dedup or silent dups.
LD4-G1 (rank3): DuckDB has no native MATERIALIZED VIEW; LD4 lists MV as feature, OT11 flags gap — cross-batch inconsistency, staleness/cost undeclared.
LD4-G2 (rank3): BATCH_SIZE 10k × 10 sessions = 100k events in memory; 500B is stored size not parse working-set (2-5KB) → OOM risk.
LD4-G3 (rank3): DuckDB single-writer + no flock; concurrent/cron/NFS ingest = corruption, not just error.
LD4-G4 (rank3): in-memory watermark checkpoint frequency undefined; crash = unbounded re-ingest (compounds LD2-G5 if idempotency broken).
OT13-G1 (rank3): OT1 repo-topology is precondition for OT13 path(1) OpenSpec; can't write changeset without repo decision.
OT13-G2 (rank3): LD2/LD4/LD5 locked pre-spike contradicts path(2) empirical validation; spike lacks authority to unlock.
OT13-G3 (rank2): path(3) keep-exploring has no exit criteria/timebox — decision debt accumulates.
OT13-G4 (rank2): OpenSpec single-change format mismatch for 13-OT+5-LD system; needs phased changesets.
X1 (rank4, cross-cutting): outbox 7d retention < processing-lag = silent permanent loss; no DLQ, no depth alert.
X2 (rank3, cross-cutting): no per-row isolation in batch; one malformed raw_command blocks 10k forever; no replay command; no backoff.
X3 (rank4, cross-cutting): clock skew across pi/zcode/hermes + 3 ts formats breaks watermarks AND time-of-day histograms; no UTC normalization layer documented.
X4 (rank4, cross-cutting): adapter schema drift upstream (pi event types, zcode/hermes schema bumps) silently corrupts analytics; no schema-version pinning or drift detection.
